answer: A conservative single-owner capability model is feasible as a finite research model. With the current whole-Euler dependency, ordinary merges usually invalidate every edge-bearing kind fact. A finer generation for a specific dominance Boolean can remain stable when Euler coordinates change. This is a non-full-invalidation opportunity, not a demonstrated profitable reuse path.
counterexample_tests_proposed_not_run: Retain raw GBotK/GTyCon unused Kind/name poisons. Right Kind WHNF and unused nextId must not become eq/hash/seq demand.
Old absence link10 followed by insert10->1 invalidates that lookup; delete/reinsert same numeric node ID gets a new incarnation. No identity-by-number reuse.
Reuse the existing actual cached-kind-edge witness: child kind2 success cannot excuse failed later edge dominance, even if kind payload is the same Star.
Keep the existing 10-node prepared-expanded-invalid case: initial actual local validation must still return the exact containment Left before any certificate use.
Invalid new root/binder prefix plus later Kind poison must return original prefix error; a certificate walk must not force the later payload.
Branch/alias/child edits creating a cycle require transitive invalidation and original colour1 check; success tickets cannot act as graph reachability proofs.
Keep dense-to-sparse and malformed raw routing controls on unchanged original path; successful dense validation alone is not canonical-map provenance.
decision: Proceed only with bounded relation-fact semantics/model design if desired; do not implement production/shadow reuse or weaken current global invalidation. Existing same-graph representation, scalar/scope-owner and small traversal NO_GO decisions remain.
independent_total_tree_controls: Two total-tree cases were subsequently executed in this symbolic model and independently checked. Source-derived Graph/unify witnesses remain unexecuted; no finer relation-ticket policy is implemented.

minimal_model.cost: Refreshing every recorded relation costs all those array reads/comparisons and relation storage, plus reverse-dependency propagation and retained Kind payloads. No proof this is cheaper than original validation, no inferred speed from profile shares, and no change to the existing global-invalidation model.
minimal_model.demand: Mint/consult metadata only behind original demanded selectors and successful prerequisite phases; metadata operations do not inspect arbitrary field values. Cached successful results retain the same opaque lazy Kind expression. Do not seq/show/hash it. Do not cache Left or exceptions. Metadata allocation/retention is observable cost and can retain old graph through a captured Kind thunk; single-owner lifetime does not prove no retention.
minimal_model.dependency_closure: Successful kind facts need transitive subfact dependencies, negative lookups, ordered branch/control dependencies, binder/parent-tag/structural-child facts and applicable relation tickets. A child kind ticket never licenses skipping a parent-specific edge check. Any changed or untracked dependency forces the original computation at its original call point.
minimal_model.global_phase: Both original and final root/member/binder/Euler prepasses remain complete. Member enumeration/ordering, raw map routing, dense/sparse choice and global errors stay global conservative dependencies. Reuse cannot suppress these checks or run before their original error prefix.
minimal_model.keys: NodeKey=(owner,logical ID,incarnation); CellKey=(NodeKey,selector); alias keys include observed absence and every link-chain lookup; fact key includes rule and ordered parameters. Checked generation counters never wrap or collide. Unknown/raw writes invalidate conservatively; exhausted model capacity is diagnostic ineligibility, not a reusable prefix.
minimal_model.minimal_safe_first_step: Model stable relation generations at the original query boundary after all original preceding gates; this alone does not skip the query. Pre-clearing an entire cached subtree by batch replay is a later separate obligation: prove all reads are total owned interval cells and cannot demand raw payload or change failure order. This review does not approve that implementation.
minimal_model.provenance: Borrow an existing cell capability only at a transformation whose actual source copies that precise field/expression. Canonical mapTag preserves constructor and leaf Kind/name origins but not automatically child expressions; new GCon mapped list is conservatively dirty. Rebinding may use the existing equality-checked branch for Binder/Flag, without adding a generic equality pass. Unknown provenance gets a fresh generation.
minimal_model.relation_refinement: After the final original prepass succeeds, only a fully defined private interval view may issue a relation ticket for the same denseContains rule and identical live endpoint parameters. Recompute the Boolean, compare with the old already-demanded Boolean, and retain its relation generation only on equality. Missing/replaced endpoints, unknown totality or different semantics make it dirty. Preserve false/unknown invalidation and original fallback; never answer from old true alone.
minimal_model.scope: One opaque generative owner for one input-to-rebuilt transaction; no persistent cross-call cache, no public raw helper changes, no StableName, no structural payload equality.

source_contract.finding: canonicalize reconstructs every Node via mapTag(resolve)/mkNode. It forces tag constructor, Arr/TyApp/Gen identities, binder Maybe head and Flag; GCon mapped child list, constructor names, leaf Kind payloads and Just binder target remain distinct lazy boundaries. equalNode/equalTag at261-262/230-258 would force additional name/kind/list content and cannot identify unchanged cells safely.

A merge deletes a loser, adds an alias and can assign winner tag/binder/flag from another input. denseFinalNode returning v means identical to its already-canonicalized skeleton node, not to the original input Node. Numeric node ID or retained skeleton pointer is insufficient provenance.

Input validation, all-equation preflight, canonicalization/rebind and final validation retain exact order. Final denseBounds and root/binder/Euler prepass cannot be replaced by the initial success. Dense-to-sparse change falls back fully. Initial prepare Right is not a certificate for an actual expanded graph.

denseContains depends on binding-tree ancestry, not stable interval numbers or only endpoint Node fields. denseKind success is Either WHNF, not forced Kind. Incoming edge gates remain separate from cached kind success; colour1 occurs check must remain before any reuse. denseStructurally tests wanted equality before require/visited and has ordered short-circuit demand.
